summary:
The Blackwater River runs about 105 miles through southeastern Virginia, from swamps near Petersburg to its confluence with the Nottoway River on the Virginia–North Carolina border, where the two form the Chowan River. The Chowan flows into Albemarle Sound.

A true blackwater river, the Blackwater has clear, tannin-stained, slightly acidic water and a swampy, mostly forested floodplain. Its wetlands include rare streamhead pocosins and old-growth bald cypress and tupelo forests, with some trees up to 800 years old. Longleaf pine flatwoods along the river support red-cockaded woodpeckers and diverse amphibians. The river is used for canoeing, kayaking and fishing.

In the 17th and 18th centuries, the river connected settlements near the James River with the Albemarle region and became an early migration and trade route south. During the Civil War, it marked part of the boundary between Union- and Confederate-held areas, and enslaved people crossed it to reach freedom. Heavy rainfall can cause rapid flooding near Zuni and Franklin, including floods in 1999 and 2006.
